comment: Metal deposit layout blueprint. Deposits are placed on concentric rings;
each ring gets countPerPlayer deposits per player slice, phase-shifted by
sliceOffset (fraction of one slice width). Per ring:
size - name from `sizes`; omit to inherit `defaultSize`. A size is the
ore body's footprint, INDEPENDENT of the flat pad under it.
dTerrainLevels - pad height in D-DEPOSIT-bar steps (METAL_DEPOSIT_STEP);
null = ride the natural terrain height under the deposit.
flatPadCells - circular flattened pad diameter in build cells; null =
auto-size to the smallest pad covering the placement disc. An explicit
value SMALLER than the footprint is legal and is the interesting case:
the pad flattens only the buildable middle and the rest of the ore
body drapes over whatever relief it crosses - down a mountain side,
across a shelf - because the ore is a shaded REGION sampled in world
XZ, not geometry. Extractors still need flat ground, so a small pad
on a big ore body is a deliberate 'one mex, lots of scenery' spot.
terrainBlendRadius - world units outside the pad where terrain eases
back to natural with a raised-cosine skirt.
depositCluster - how each ring origin expands into deposits. Two types:
type 'group-ring' (default when omitted): count deposits on a circle
of radius around the origin; angleOffset is radians relative to the
origin's radial angle from map center. Each deposit is a standalone
pad - overlapping pads at different heights cliff (closest wins).
type 'group-manual': one deposit per authored spot, and the group is
ONE TERRAIN UNIT. Spots use one of two addressing forms (never mix):
OFFSET spots {x, y} - world-unit offsets in the origin's radial
frame (+x away from map center, +y perpendicular), so every player's
slice keeps the same local shape. RING-COORDINATE spots
{radiusFraction, sliceOffset} - placed by the exact same oval/slice
formula as a standalone ring, so merging existing rings into one
group keeps their positions identical for every player count and
map size (ring must author countPerPlayer 1). Each spot may author
its own dTerrainLevels (omit = inherit ring, null = natural height),
its own flatPadCells (omit = inherit ring), and its own size.
Terrain: every deposit's flat pad stays perfectly flat at its own
height; the union of the group's flat pads is fully overridden by
one smoothed field that cosine-interpolates between the plateaus;
the whole field eases back to natural terrain over
terrainBlendRadius. Use this when large pads must sit near each
other at different heights without cliffing.
sizesComment: Authored ore-body size classes. Two numbers, and they mean exactly what
they say:
metalCellCount - how many metal build cells this ore body owns. Not a
side length, not a target to approximate: the placer lands this many
cells or the config is rejected.
placementRadiusCells - the radius, in build cells from the deposit's
origin cell, of the disc those cells are ALLOWED to land in. Nothing
outside it can ever be metal.
Inside the disc the cells are scattered statistically rather than grown
outward from the centre, so an ore body has no connectivity rule and no
square footprint. A cell's chance of being metal is a raised cosine of
its distance from the origin: 1.0 dead centre, 0.5 at half the radius,
0.0 at the rim. Draws never repeat a cell, so the whole authored count
always lands - a crowded core just pushes the remainder further out.
The two numbers together set how the body READS. The disc holds about
0.297 * pi * r^2 cells' worth of cosine probability; asking for roughly
1.5x that (the authored classes all sit near 1.47-1.6) gives a solid
core that frays into scattered specks near the rim. Push the radius up
and the same count thins into a dusting; pull it down and the body
hardens into a disc. The classes differ in scale, not in character.
BUILD_GRID_CELL_SIZE is 20 world units, so 'titanic' reaches 76 cells =
1520 units from its origin.
Neither number can move a deposit: it snaps to the centre of the build
cell its ring point landed in, reading nothing from the size class. A
size is free to be any positive integer.
productionNominalCellsComment: Economy calibration only: an extractor's metal rate is its blueprint production divided by this many cells, times the metal cells its footprint actually covers. Deliberately NOT tied to a size class - retuning a size must not silently retune the economy. Note that a cosine-scattered body is not solid: an extractor over the core covers fewer metal cells than its footprint has cells, and closing that gap means lowering placementRadiusCells, not raising this.
surfaceFieldComment: The rendered ore region. Deposit cells are baked once, at match start,
into a whole-map signed-distance field the terrain fragment shader samples
by world XZ. Nothing here is simulation state: the authoritative metal
cells remain each deposit's own cell list, and the field never enters the
canonical state hash.
texelWorldSize - target world units per field texel.
maxTextureDimension - hard cap per axis; the largest authored maps
coarsen the texel size rather than allocate an unbounded texture.
edgeRangeWorldUnits - the +/- distance the byte encoding spans. Past it
the stored distance SATURATES, so anything reading the field further
out reads a value that has stopped varying. It therefore has to cover
the whole reach of the ore-edge treatment in colorsConfig
(environment.metalDeposit.edge), not just the contour - a dirt band
running past the encoding ends in a perfect circle at the radius it
ran out. Pinned by contract test. Byte resolution is the only cost of
widening it, and at 10 world units per texel the field is nowhere
near limited by that.
smoothPasses - separable 1-2-1 passes over the DISTANCE values, which
rounds the 20-unit build-cell staircase into a curve.
edgeFeatherWorldUnits - 0 gives a crisp, screen-space anti-aliased ore
edge; larger values fade ore into the surrounding ground.
